speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what were the challenges experienced during the firefighting operation on 8 December 2022 which resulted in the passing of an SCDF NSF firefighter; and (b) how does SCDF ensure that its frontline officers are adequately trained and equipped to carry out their duties safely and effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I invite the Member to seek clarifications, if need be.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If the Member's questions have been addressed, it may not be necessary for the Member to proceed with his question at the subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The safety of all Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) personnel is of utmost importance to the Home Team.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The FFC includes both theoretical and practical components, and a series of proficiency and certification tests.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These include the Individual Physical Proficiency Test, Breathing Apparatus Proficiency Test, Hazmat Responder Certification Test, Firemanship Skills Assessment and a written test on basic firemanship, rescue and equipment knowledge.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to the skills taught in the FFC, Regular Servicemen and NSFs who are appointed to leadership roles will undergo a Section Commander or Rota Commander Course, which trains them to lead a section comprising three to four personnel, or a Rota which is a duty shift comprising several sections.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Firefighting training at the CDA is conducted with "live" fire simulators to provide realism, so that trainees gain experience operating in conditions similar to real-life firefighting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF has protocols to ensure that the training curriculum is reviewed regularly to ensure currency.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After graduating from the CDA, training continues to be an integral part of a firefighter's daily routine, including NSF firefighters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Firefighters undergo exercises and drills during each shift, to familiarise themselves with their respective roles and functions as part of a crew, as well as to maintain individual fitness and competencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They must also undergo annual proficiency tests conducted by CDA to ensure that their skills and fitness levels meet the required standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In a fire emergency, NSF firefighters and NSF section commanders are deployed alongside Regular Servicemen in a section.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: NSmen and Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU) volunteer firefighters may also be deployed within the section.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Depending on the scale of the emergency, the task force that is activated may comprise several sections.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The task force is led by a ground commander, who is responsible for leading the operation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The ground commander will monitor and direct the operation, and request for more resources as reinforcement, if necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All firefighting Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) used by SCDF are certified according to relevant international standards, such as the American National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards and European standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about the challenges experienced by the SCDF during the firefighting operation on 8 December 2022.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While responding to the incident, the SCDF officers found the fire engine accessway leading to Block 91 Henderson Road obstructed by a tent where a funeral wake was being held.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The officers removed the bollards that were padlocked to the ground near the tentage to create an access path.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: About 40% of the responders were NSmen – meaning the majority, 60% of the responders were Regular Officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Police are currently conducting an independent, thorough investigation into the circumstances of SGT1 Edward's demise and will apprise the Coroner of its findings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At this stage, it is premature to determine the factors which contributed to SGT1 Edward's death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Coroner will consider the Police's investigation findings, in determining the cause of death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Due to the ongoing investigations, we are unable to share further details at this stage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF will seek to understand what had happened, including if standard operating procedures and protocols had been followed, and how these may need to be tightened to keep the officers as safe as possible when they serve our nation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And I hope that the family of SGT1 Edward Go would be supported whilst they come to terms with their loss and, in time, heal.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My question for the hon Minister of State is in relation to the deployment of NSmen.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Minister of State mentioned that the ratio of NSmen deployment for that particular incident was 40:60, 60% Regulars.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Having regard to the fact that NSmen generally have less experience than Regulars, may I ask whether there is a certain strategy to better protect NSmen?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And in respect of SGT1 Edward Go, I understand that investigations are ongoing, but will the hon Minister of State reveal the extent of training that he had for the fire incident that he was called to fight?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: An NSF's journey with SCDF starts from his enlistment into the SCDF where he receives basic, and subsequently, vocational training appropriate for his PES condition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, at the start of his enlistment, we already looked at it on how that journey is going to be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: NSFs who are assigned in the operational roles, as I shared earlier, are given robust and realistic training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They also use proper PPE and equipment that are common to their fire station.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: From their time in the CDA, their instructors will closely monitor them and look at their progress and help build their confidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The relationship, the camaraderie and peer support are also vital parts of the culture and overall journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, I visit SCDF fire stations as well as some of the set-ups regularly, and this is something I have noticed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The peer support, the relationship and that journey that someone goes through – whether for NSFs or Regulars – is so important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The juniors will look up to the seniors, not only between the Regulars and the NSFs, but also between the NSFs together – they look up to their seniors and they want to see how they can play their part.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: After posting to a fire station, they will be assigned support appliances.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They will not straightaway go to the frontline, as in, to fight the fire.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is the opportunity to give them the time to settle down and get to know their Rota.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: During this time, their supervisors will observe the NSFs in the daily shifts, watch them perform during drills and training to assess their suitability, competency and confidence to be placed on turn-out, on the main fire engines and Red Rhinos.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is where they are most likely to be on-scene, earlier than the rest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also look at the composition of the crew, where we carefully balance it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The supervisor will ensure that there is a good mix of experienced and seniority, while still giving NSF firefighters the opportunity to grow from accumulating turn-out experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, just like many of the vocations which require practical experience, the only way for all firefighting personnel – whether Regular or NSF – to build their experience is on-the-job training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This takes place under close supervision with multiple layers of safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we ensure the training that they receive, the PPE that they wear and the colleagues they turn-out with.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Like I shared earlier, this is something which is very obvious when you speak and talk to them about operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is something that we are very proud of in our SCDF officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the late SGT1 Edward Go, this is something that I would like to share, even though the investigations are still ongoing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Like what the Member shared earlier, we feel the loss of the late SGT1 Edward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Just like the rest, all NSFs need to be certified medically fit and complete the relevant training and courses, prior to deployment at the frontline.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Like the rest, he would have gone through the journey like any other SCDF NSF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, he was an officer with some level of experience as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My deepest condolences to the family of the late SGT1 Edward Go.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I note that there have been quite a number of fires in public rental blocks in recent years.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And if so, what are the mitigating measures that can be taken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the unit level, flats are designed as separate fire compartments to minimise the risk of fire spread to other units via walls of required fire-resistance rating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And fire-rated doors will also have a closer, to ensure that they do not stay open after the occupants have evacuated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This maintains the route of evacuation for residents for a certain time, based on the fire rating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the common areas of Block 91 Henderson Road, the corridor width complies with the prevailing Fire Code requirements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While some rental blocks are maybe more densely occupied than some of the sold blocks, this does not compromise their compliance with the Fire Code.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And also if Members remember, during a Sitting a few months ago, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and I also answered two queries as to how we would want to make sure that the fire safety in the HDB blocks are enhanced.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Beyond the infrastructure, we also work with community organisations and grassroots organisations to see how we can enhance the community resilience, with regards to how they can keep their homes safe from fires.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And when fires happen, what we can do as a community to see how we can get everyone to a safe place, while the SCDF and other agencies do their work to help solve the issue.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, he mentioned that the Coroner would study the outcome of the Police investigations into the incident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Under section 20 of the Coroners Act, if I am not mistaken, the Coroner may carry out such an inquiry, if that is necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, if there is a need for the Coroner to do so, it will be done.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will see how the Police investigations go.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I will not make any assumptions or speculation regarding the investigation.
